notes: The feed registry as data. Which group carries which feed, on which ports, with which published
set of channels, is the publisher's to decide and it changes without our involvement. This
document is supplied to the container at runtime (--feed-registry-url, --feed-registry) and this
copy is only the compiled-in fallback, so the container runs standalone and has a
last-known-good to fall back to when a fetch fails.
The authoritative fleet list is the feed-capture recorder inventory in the private infra repo,
NOT the publisher deployment inventory - the latter covers only a subset of the hosts on the
group. Sourcing this table from the deployment inventory alone is what left five blocks unbound
and the bridge ingesting about a third of the group's datagrams.
The venue is resolved per message from the wire SourceID (see processor.rs), so the `venue`
below is only the default for SourceIDs the registry does not assign. The wire value is
authoritative: a publisher stamping an ID that is not its own is a publisher defect and is
corrected at the publisher, never remapped here.
A `code` that does not match the live group fails silently: `doublezero status --json` reports
no match, the reconciler never activates the row, and there is no warning and no failed bind -
just a receiver that never starts. A wrong port fails the same way, one layer down.
`sources` is the Source ID -> registry-name allocation, generated from
edge-feed-spec/sources/spec.md, which stays the sole authority for it. Assigning a venue is a
republish of this document rather than a code change and a release. The block is optional: a
document written before it existed is legal and resolves against the compiled-in table in
sources.rs instead, which is also the fallback when a URL fetch degrades. A name is emitted
verbatim as `venue`/`source_name` on the wire and as every `venue=` metric label value, so it
must be uppercase, and an id or a name may appear only once - two sources sharing either would
collapse to one identity and the arbiter keys dedup on (venue, symbol). An id this block does
not assign is NOT an error: the wire Source ID is authoritative and gets a distinct synthesized
SOURCE_<id> label, bounded by MAX_UNREGISTERED_SOURCES. Id 0 and the SOURCE_<id>/UNREGISTERED
names are reserved for that fallback and are refused here.
ORDERING. A binary that predates this block ignores it and validates rows against its own
compiled-in table, so under a URL origin a row naming a source only this block assigns is
rejected and the WHOLE document degrades to that binary's built-in copy - losing every other
change in the same republish. Until the fleet is upgraded, only name sources every deployed
binary already resolves.
`publishers` is a tagged union. `explicit` carries port blocks verbatim; `derived` carries a
published set of channels plus per-role bases and expands to `base + id` per channel, one
publisher per channel.
Adding a field is NOT a version bump. The loader has no deny_unknown_fields anywhere: an unknown
key is warned about by path and ignored, so an additive republish reaches an older fleet without
a rebuild - which is what every caller depends on. `version` bumps only for a change that
reinterprets what an existing field MEANS, since that is what an older binary would read
wrongly. A missing REQUIRED field stays fatal, so a typo cannot quietly default.

notes: Confirmed on-wire (group-bound capture) plus the publisher fleet's port blocks: eleven
publishers - six DoubleZero hosts, four partners and one unattributed.
Base ports follow no arithmetic rule. The v0.7 publisher takes an arbitrary mkt_port per
channel, so a block can sit anywhere (9011 is base+10, not base+N*100). The one guarantee
is the spacing within a block: +1/+2 for this publisher role. Derive a block from its
market-data port; never derive the market-data port from an index.

notes: Market-by-Order on the same group, one port block per publisher (paired with the
top-of-book row above). Depth-only: top of book owns this venue's trades.
Unconfirmed ports and how each one fails, since the failure is NOT uniform: dz_receiver_up
is driven by the idle watchdog, which tracks the mktdata port only.
- wrong mktdata  -> no datagrams -> dz_receiver_up == 0. Visible.
- wrong refdata  -> RefDataState never resolves a definition and every processor gates
emission on one, so the receiver reads healthy and emits nothing.
- wrong snapshot -> books stay Recovering forever, so the publisher contributes no depth
while still reading healthy.
The only signal for the latter two is dz_datagrams_received_total{role} pinned at 0.
Both feeds must list the same publishers: a publisher onboarded to one and forgotten on the
other shows up in production as a venue missing depth for one mirror.

notes: Moved from the pre-launch scottsdale/233.84.178.18 location to the ledger-registered
edge-phoenix-tob group on 2026-09-01; the old group is dead and a row carrying it
activates nothing, silently. A single publisher on 9201/9202, from the publisher's own
deploy unit and confirmed on the live wire 2026-09-01: two 30-minute captures matched
3,518 + 3,188 fills 1:1 against the venue's public API with zero price/size/side
mismatches.
Refdata stamps Channel ID 1 (wire-confirmed 2026-09-01; schema v3). That must agree with
the MBP sibling's refdata channel: the instrument catalog is keyed on the refdata
channel, so a divergence would list every Phoenix product twice and turn the bare
PHOENIX:SYMBOL product ids ambiguous. The 2026-06-30 fixture shows the OLD publisher
(schema v1) stamped refdata on channel 2 - re-capture both refdata roles if either feed's
channel numbering changes.
Market-by-price sibling of edge-phoenix-tob: same publisher process, same manifest and
instrument ids, schema v3, Channel ID 1 on all three roles (wire-confirmed 2026-09-01 -
see the top-of-book row's channel note; the catalog depends on the two refdata channels
agreeing). Ports are the publisher's --mbp-* defaults, confirmed on the live wire
2026-09-01: books synced end-to-end and prices validated against the top-of-book quotes
and the public API. Both Phoenix rows claim the tape (this feed's mktdata role carries
Trade byte-identical to top-of-book's); the reconciler ranks TopOfBook over
MarketByPrice when both run, and the moment of overlap at a handover is collapsed by the
trade_id dedup window - which requires Phoenix's real venue trade ids: a publisher change
to the trade_id == 0 sentinel would double-print at every ownership transfer, since the
Coordinated no-id guard forwards a conflicting zero-id pair rather than dropping it.
Perps, two separately-gated groups: edge-kalshi-perps-tob carries top of book and edge-kalshi-perps-mbp the
market-by-price book. Both claim the tape - a host holding only edge-kalshi-perps-mbp must still serve
`trade` - and which of them prints is the reconciler's runtime decision.
`code` is transcribed verbatim from what the DoubleZero ledger registers today, never from
what reads better here: it is matched against what `doublezero status --json` reports, so a
prettier code matches nothing and activates nothing. All three Kalshi codes were moved to
the edge-kalshi-{perps,sports}-{tob,mbp} strings the ledger rename registered; until that
edit the three rows had been dark since the rename, with no warning and no failed bind.
`venue` is independent of `code` - it is the source-registry name for the Source ID these
rows carry. The pre-launch codename is no longer accepted on input anywhere: nothing feeds
it in now that the ledger strings have moved.
Both groups are live on testnet and mainnet as of 2026-08-07; a permanently-zero
dz_receiver_up here means a transcription slip, not a quiet feed.
PORT PROVENANCE. Every port in this document was confirmed against a live packet capture on
2026-08-09, because ALL THREE rows were found misprovisioned that day and the build was green
throughout. This row carried 7576/7577 and the market-by-price sibling carried 31000/41000/
51000 - i.e. each row was authored one port block off, taking the ports that belong to a
sibling.
Nothing internal could detect it: the test that exists to pin these rows 'against the
deployment' asserted the code matched itself. A port here is a claim about a machine outside
this process, so it is verified from outside - by capture, or by the publishers' own
deployment inventory - or it is marked unverified. Never by reading prose that describes an
allocation; read the values the publisher actually renders.
One publisher per row: the two paths share a port block and are distinguished, for
producer-side state (RefDataState, sequence tracking), only by datagram source IP address.
MIRROR. A second publisher mirrors the whole published set on that SAME port block, stamping
every wire channel_id raised by 100 - confirmed live on 2026-08-11 from a product catalog
listing every market twice, at channel N and channel N+100. publisher_offset records that
for ingest: it canonicalises the mirror's channel id back to the base publisher's for
catalog/history identity ONLY, never for the per-publisher book and sequence state above,
which stays keyed on the raw wire channel id and the per-publisher split.
The market-by-price block is spaced +10000 / +20000, not the +1 / +2 the Hyperliquid
publisher role uses.
Mirrored exactly like the edge-kalshi-perps-tob top-of-book sibling: a second publisher on the same
port block, channel_id raised by 100. See edge-kalshi-perps-tob's MIRROR note.
A disjoint universe under the same Source ID as the perps rows, which is exactly what
`category` exists to express: these markets mirror nothing of the perps ones, so the two
must never contest each other's tape or book. Never argue that separation from channel-id
ranges - the upstream allocation is mid-migration and any numeric gap between the universes
is a coincidence of current numbering, owned upstream and enforced nowhere in our code.
PUBLISHED SET. One channel is a league or a sport, and each is an independent state machine with
its own Reset Count, sequence series, Manifest Seq and snapshot cycle - so one channel maps
to one publisher and therefore one receiver task with its own processor state and books.
Ids are permanent from first publication: promoting a competition out of a tag channel takes
a free id rather than renumbering. 30-38 are reserved for exactly those promotions and are
not published. 63 and 120 were retired on 2026-08-08 and are never reissued (120
additionally falls inside the second publisher's +100 range). An id listed here that the
publisher does not send binds a socket that stays silent, which reads as a dead publisher.
PORTS. base + channel_id on all three port roles - the property the publisher's own
validate_port_scheme asserts. A subscriber that computes it differently joins the right
group and hears silence.
These bases are what the publishers are configured with, confirmed against the deployment
that check - 33000/43000 is the top-of-book sibling's base, and a market-by-price row built
on it joins the right group and receives nothing, which reads as a dead publisher rather
than as a misconfiguration. The same allocation has been decided several times upstream in
dated specs, each reversing the last, which is why it lives here and not in compiled code:
correcting it is an edit to this document, not a rebuild.
DEPLOYMENT. One publisher per channel and no failover today. A second publisher takes this
same published set with every id offset by +100, leaving the ports untouched - the port names the
league so a subscriber binds one socket per league and hears both publishers on it, while
channel_id names the league AND the publisher so the two are sequenced separately.
publisher_offset records that +100 for ingest: it canonicalises the mirror's channel id back
to the league's for catalog/history/book identity ONLY, never for the per-publisher book and
sequence state that has to stay separate. The top-of-book sibling on group 233.84.178.17 is
not yet published, which is why this document carries no row for it.
SOURCE IP ADDRESSES. Two, confirmed by a warehouse capture on 2026-08-11: both publishers
carry the WHOLE published set, mirroring each other, and are separated by the channel offset above.
An earlier capture (2026-08-09) saw one address and the note here said so; the second host
came up between them, so treat any count recorded here as of its date and re-measure.
That two-publisher shape is the one the book gate is built for - it elects one per
(venue, category) and drops the peer's copy. What would break it is a publisher PER CHANNEL,
since 31 addresses on one (venue, category) would leave one channel served and thirty
dropped. That is not the deployment: the published set is mirrored, not sharded.
